thesis: Xylem Inc. (XYL) is a global water technology company that designs, manufactures, and services pumps, treatment equipment, smart meters, analytics software, and outsourced water solutions for utilities and industrial customers. **[Fact]** The company reports four segments: **Water Infrastructure** ($2,636 million revenue in 2025), **Applied Water** ($1,849 million), **Measurement and Control Solutions** ($2,086 million), and **Water Solutions and Services** ($2,464 million). **[Fact]** FY2025 consolidated revenue was **$9.035 billion** (+5.5% versus $8.562 billion in 2024), operating income **$1,223 million** (13.5% margin), and free cash flow approximately **$910 million** (operating cash flow $1,241 million minus capital spending $331 million). **[Fact]** The Evoqua Water Technologies merger closed **May 24, 2023**, creating the WSS segment and roughly doubling the company's services exposure. Xylem sells through direct utility channels, industrial distributors, and recurring service contracts under brands including Flygt, Goulds, Sensus, Wedeco, and Godwin.
why_market_wrong: The market may treat Xylem as a slow-growth industrial and underweight the post-Evoqua margin trajectory and debt paydown. **[Fact]** Adjusted operating income rose to **$1,612 million** (17.8% margin) in 2025 from **$1,373 million** (16.0%) in 2024; Water Infrastructure operating margin expanded to **17.5%** from **13.9%** and WSS to **12.3%** from **9.3%**. **[Fact]** Long-term debt fell to **$1,408 million** from **$1,978 million** year over year while cash rose to **$1,479 million**. **[Inference]** Generalists may anchor on Measurement segment margin compression (11.7% operating margin versus 13.2% prior year) and premium valuation multiples, missing that consolidated owner cash is growing through mix and integration. There is no dated catalyst; the inefficiency is **descriptive** (quality water compounder at a full price), not an equity yield curve setup.
